record_type_quote: One study has systematically explored the effects of frontal eye field tDCS on eye movements (Kanai et al., 2012, Front. Pscyhiatry). They showed that anodal tDCS of the frontal eye field can decrease the median latency of saccades, specifically when saccades were made to targets in the visual hemifield contralateral to the stimulated hemisphere. In the present study, we aimed to replicate and extend this result with a similar experiment.

targets.outcome_quote: Our initial results show that we are unable to reproduce the effect found by Kanai et al.: neither form of tDCS affected the median latency of contra- or ipsilateral saccades. This result suggests that oculomotor functions of the frontal eye fields may not be robustly amenable to tDCS.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Fresh sample of 15 participants fails to reproduce the specified saccade latency effect. Larger ongoing sample is future work.
